summary: Re-sending the same validated draft after the previous turn's final response failed JSON parsing (unescaped quotes inside the summary string). The draft is unchanged and still validates: it closes the read-index thread and opens a new investigation on participant eligibility, testing whether a node the configuration no longer contains can still have proposals accepted. Two source facts anchor it: node.run disables the proposal channel when the node learns it was removed but re-enables it on any observed leader change, with an in-tree comment conceding the logic is not sound; and neither stepFollower's forward path nor stepLeader's MsgProp handler checks sender membership. A focused probe against the real FSM confirmed both halves - after applyConfChange removed node 3 from a leader's config a MsgProp with From=3 was accepted with no error and appended one entry, and a removed follower still forwarded a local MsgProp to its leader. The record is a behaviour fact plus one open necessary gap, with the interpretation deliberately left conditional and unresolved because the decisive question is whether the library owes sender eligibility or the application owns that authorization. No defect is asserted there and severity is not assessed; the retry-growth finding and its measurements are unchanged.
